reelection.rule: Rule: next even-year November for this House term. legislators-current.yaml ends the current term on 2027-01-03. The even-year November before that January 3 end is November 2026. The file has no election day, so no day of the month is shown.

votes.plain_language: Official question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended. H.R. 9612: American Enrichment Deployment Act. Result: Passed.

votes.bill_title: Nuclear REFUEL (Recycling Efficient Fuels Utilizing Expedited Licensing) Act
votes.plain_language: Official question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended. H.R. 3978: Nuclear REFUEL (Recycling Efficient Fuels Utilizing Expedited Licensing) Act. Result: Passed.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — Ratepayer Protection Act (H R 9340)
votes.plain_language: This bill tells state utility regulators to consider making very large power users, such as data centers using 100 megawatts or more, pay the full extra cost of grid upgrades built to serve them. A two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Passage — Protecting Domestic Mining Act (H R 1501)
votes.plain_language: This bill puts mining infrastructure projects into the FAST Act's faster environmental-review process and blocks a proposed rule that would have limited which mining projects qualify. A Yea passes it. A Nay votes no.

votes.question: On Passage — HEATS Act (H R 5587)
votes.plain_language: This bill exempts certain geothermal activities on state and private lands (except Indian lands) from drilling permit requirements as well as environmental and historic preservation review requirements. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Passage — Reliable Federal Infrastructure Act (H R 4690)
votes.plain_language: This bill repeals certain energy efficiency performance standards for new federal buildings and federal buildings undergoing major renovations. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Recommit — Reliable Federal Infrastructure Act (H R 4690)
votes.plain_language: H.R. 4690 (Reliable Federal Infrastructure Act) repeals certain energy efficiency performance standards for new federal buildings and federal buildings undergoing major renovations. A motion to recommit is the minority's last formal chance to send a bill back to committee before the passage vote. A Yea supports sending it back; a Nay keeps it on the floor for the passage vote.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass — To require the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission to extend the time period during which licensees are required to commence construction of certain hydropower projects (S 1020)
votes.bill_title: A bill to require the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission to extend the time period during which licensees are required to commence construction of certain hydropower projects.
votes.plain_language: This bill authorizes the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission to extend construction deadlines for hydropower projects that were issued a license before March 13, 2020. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Passage — Homeowner Energy Freedom Act (H R 4758)
votes.plain_language: This bill repeals three Department of Energy programs: high-efficiency electric home rebates for certain low- or moderate-income households, state-based home energy efficiency contractor training grants, and assistance for states and localities to adopt specified building energy codes. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.plain_language: H.R. 4758 (Homeowner Energy Freedom Act) repeals three Department of Energy programs: high-efficiency electric home rebates for certain low- or moderate-income households, state-based home energy efficiency contractor training grants, and assistance for states and localities to adopt specified building energy codes. posts.text: Today, I proudly celebrate the 50th anniversary of Prison Fellowship, Second Chance Month, and the introduction of the Second Chance Month Resolution. Second chances help individuals rebuild their lives, strengthen families, and make communities safer. https://t.co/DEoFDPQRqk

January isn't just a new year; it’s a time to prioritize our well-being. This month, I’m highlighting: Cervical Health & Glaucoma screenings, Birth Defects prevention & education, Stalking awareness & survivor support the urgent need for blood donors. https://t.co/DPvWRQrRsC

Rep. Danny K. Davis joined Illinois’ Democratic congressional delegation in demanding the Trump Administration immediately comply with federal law and release $1 BILLION in frozen funding for child care and essential services. https://t.co/MYn2lHSKln

Today, we honor Dr. King not with words, but with service. As we face renewed attacks on our democracy, we remember that progress is never inevitable. Let’s organize and recommit to the "Beloved Community" he envisioned. https://t.co/vLb3Il0dbq

This week, I fought to hold HHS accountable for illegally halting $10 b for child care & services in IL, MN, CA, CO, & NY and child care funds across the US. The GOP rejected my effort to penalize HHS’s illegal actions. Thank you AG Raoul for suing to stop the cruel GOP efforts. https://t.co/uG32JwsSh7

Thousands of children and families are being harmed out of political revenge. It’s unpresidential and un-American, yet HHS has illegally stopped $1 b of our funds.

HHS must immediately release the $1 b in child care and social services funding that our state is rightfully owed. https://t.co/0b7fUVNqrv

ACA Extension: Today’s victory proves a simple truth: when Democrats stay unified, listen to the people, & remain focused on results, we win. A people united will never be defeated. Democrats are on a roll! We are fighting for ordinary, everyday Americans. https://t.co/N1GNsNnmKe

Congressman Danny Davis: I have no respect for authoritarian rule, anywhere.
President Trump does not get to decide war, choose foreign leaders, or bypass Congress.
That’s not democracy. That’s executive overreach. https://t.co/v3LEwijbnN

January is #NationalMentoringMonth. I’ve always said that our youth are the best of who we are. To everyone in the 7th District who takes the time to guide, teach, and inspire a young person: Thank you. You are building the future of Chicago.  #MentorshipMatters #BeAMentor #IL07 https://t.co/FP5gYzN4La

As we enter 2026, I remain more committed than ever to fighting for our youth, expanding healthcare, and creating opportunity for all. Wishing you a year filled with peace, health, and progress. Let’s keep moving forward together! #HappyNewYear #Chicago #Service https://t.co/XSkPeRxbgs

Wishing all my constituents a peaceful holiday season. It remains a distinct honor to serve as your Representative in Congress. May the spirit of community stay with you and your families throughout the coming year. https://t.co/X0K836vIK7

The U.S. Department of Justice's opinion declaring Minority Serving Institution programs unconstitutional denies both the constitutionality and the necessity of targeted efforts designed to expand educational access for historically marginalized communities. https://t.co/lKl99SEvjj

I’m joining my Democratic colleagues to demand House Republicans vote NOW to extend ACA tax credits. GOP inaction means health insurance premiums will skyrocket on Jan 1. We need a clean extension today to keep healthcare affordable. 📉🏥 #Healthcare #ACA https://t.co/PvJXSDwrJ1

I am very honored that the American Ambulance Association presented me with a beautiful award for my strong support for emergency medical services.  These wonderful professionals do amazing work for our communities. https://t.co/PCLLgP4FZ1

I am deeply honored to have received a Hill Champion award from the National Minority AIDS Council.  We must continue to sustain and grow federal funding for HIV prevention, treatment, research, and community engagement. https://t.co/Lmt2Uuzp6B

Antisemitic violence at Bondi Beach and the tragedy at Brown University are attacks on our democratic values. Hate has no place in our democracy. Congressman Danny K. Davis remains committed to protecting civil rights and keeping our communities safe. https://t.co/ZA9BIidfJ8

A filing lists assets, income, liabilities, and trades the member reported; it is not proof of a conflict or of wrongdoing. Dollar ranges and asset names are in the PDF. funding.heading: Disclosed campaign receipts
funding.detail: Federal cards show the principal campaign committee and OpenFEC totals for one two-year cycle, plus itemized Schedule A contributors. House uses 2026. Senate uses the cycle of the next election (2026, 2028, or 2030). This is not career fundraising and does not include Schedule E outside spending. Governors do not get a federal contribution list.
